full_judgment:
This Rule, at the instance of the plaintiff, is directed against the judgment and decree dated 22-11-87, passed by the Subordinate judge, Rajshahi in Title Appeal No. 4 of 1985 affirming those dated 17-12-84 of Munsif, Sadar Rajshahi in OC suit No. 573 of 1980. 

 3. Mr Sultan Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioner, submits that in view of the fact that the plaintiff has proved title and exclusive possession in the suit and that the defendant has failed to prove this title and possession in the suit sand, the court below acted illegally in not decreeing the suit. The learned Advocate further submits that possession of the petitioner having been established by cogent evidence the courts below erred in law in not decreeing the suit instead of holding the petitioner as a trespasser having no title to the suit land. 

 "Failure to prove title by the plaintiff in a suit for permanent injunction cannot disentitle him to a decree for permanent injunction if he can prove possession. 

 The plaintiff has not produced the original sale deed dated 4-2-75 executed by Razia Khatun in favour of the plaintiff and the plaintiff has failed to prove his title to the suit premises but both the courts below have found possession of the suit premises in favour of the plaintiff. The court below erred in law in not decreeing the suit on proof of possession of the plaintiff. In the face of payment of rent on mutation and taxes in respect of the suit land and possession thereof, the question of title is not that material in a suit for permanent injunction and even if the plaintiff is is possession without any title he is entitled to an order of injunction from the court of law, The aggrieved party may however get his title declared and recover possession of the suit land from the plaintiff in a proper proceeding. Reference may also be had to the cases of Abdul Kader Mondal and others; reported in 47 DLR 237 and Palyan Krishna Goswami vs. Madhya Para High School 1995 (15) BLD 509. 

 8. Both the courts below having found the possession in favour of the plaintiffs and the plaintiff having proved his exclusive possession in the suit land is entitled to a decree for permanent injunction restraining the defendants from entering into the suit premises and taking possession thereof except in due process of law. 

 9. In view of the about the impugned judgment and decree of the courts below are not sustainable in law and the same are set aside. The suit is accordingly decreed restraining the defendant from entering into the suit premises and taking possession there of except in due process of land.
